questions.prompt: Which features help make Earth suitable for life? Choose all that apply.
options: A magnetic field and ozone layer that shield harmful radiation
questions.explain: Earth isn’t the largest planet; Jupiter is.

questions.prompt: What is the ‘Goldilocks zone’ around a star?
options: Where planets are made of gold
The range of distances where it's not too hot or too cold for liquid water
questions.explain: Liquid water is key to life as we know it.

questions.prompt: In the Goldilocks Lab, Earth with NO atmosphere was frozen. What does this show?
options: Earth is too close to the Sun
Earth’s natural greenhouse effect keeps it warm enough for liquid water
questions.explain: Greenhouse gases add about 33 °C of warming.

questions.prompt: Why is Venus so hot even though it is further from the Sun than Mercury?
options: Its very thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat (a runaway greenhouse effect)
It is closer to the Sun than Mercury
questions.explain: Too much greenhouse gas makes a planet far too hot.

questions.prompt: Without its atmosphere, Earth’s average temperature would be about −18 °C. The greenhouse effect adds about 33 °C. What is the actual average?
Does each action help protect Earth’s life-support systems or harm them?

items.label: Switching to solar and wind power

questions.explain: Our actions affect the atmosphere, water and living things that keep Earth habitable.

questions.prompt: Using ideas from this topic, explain why adding extra greenhouse gases to the atmosphere is a problem, and suggest two actions your family or school could take.
questions.modelAnswer: The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth at about 15 °C, but extra carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels traps more heat and raises temperatures. This causes more heatwaves, changing monsoons, melting glaciers in the Himalayas and rising seas. Actions: walk, cycle or use public transport instead of cars; switch off lights and fans when not needed and use LED bulbs; plant trees; install solar panels on the school roof.
rubric: Two practical actions linked to reducing emissions
questions.explain: Criterion D: connect science to responsible action.

questions.text: The ___ layer high in the atmosphere protects life by absorbing harmful ultraviolet rays from the Sun.
questions.explain: CFCs damaged the ozone layer; the Montreal Protocol is helping it recover.
